summary: Giles County, VA: a lookout also called Sugar Run, still standing per USGS notes in 1934, 1952 and 1964; now listed as gone. Summit has communication towers.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone. The last dated mention, from 1964, says the tower was still standing.

access.note: Reached on foot from the Appalachian Trail; the site describes a short unmarked side trail to the summit.

visit.trail_note: The AT detour is listed as 0.2 mile with a 40 foot gain. The side trail to the summit takes about 5 minutes.

events.note: A USGS party set a benchmark at the summit, about 90 yards east of the Flat Top Fire Tower, so the tower was already standing.
USGS returned and noted the lookout tower still there.
USGS found the tower still standing, but its measurements suggested it could have been moved a short distance.

evidence.quote: Located at the head of Sugar Run, this tower was at the junction of Pearis, Sugar Run and Flat Top Mountains.

notes_for_editor: Only one history source (a hiker's site quoting USGS survey notes from 1934, 1952 and 1964) plus the FFLA list. No build date, builder, operator or staffing found; the story leaves those out. Sources use both Flat Top and Sugar Run; the record name is kept. The brief's status, county and coordinates match. Searches used: 2. Pages read: 2 plus the FFLA list.
